item.title: El Nino crisis: Water and food shortage hits Dom Kagul in SSY
item.description: Communities in the mountain villages of Dom Kagul, Kamtai District in Sinasina-Yongomugl are facing severe water shortage and famine as the El Nino dry spell continues to worsen. A local community leader, Dom David Kua from Dom Kagul village, said after a prolonged dry season, villages that once had abundant food and coffee along the Wahgi River are now struggling to survive.
item.content:encoded:
Communities in the mountain villages of Dom Kagul, Kamtai District in Sinasina-Yongomugl are facing severe water shortage and famine as the El Nino dry spell continues to worsen.

A local community leader, Dom David Kua from Dom Kagul village, said after a prolonged dry season, villages that once had abundant food and coffee along the Wahgi River are now struggling to survive.

He said villages on both sides of the Wahgi River bordering Gumine and Sinasina-Yongomugl Districts including Konoma, Dom Kagul, Gunangi and towards Ubanidiawa are experiencing the same situation.

"On the mountaintops, all our water holes and creeks have dried up. Even the Wahgi River is drying up. We have no water to drink and our people are starving," Kua said.

Kua added that a number of people are now suffering from diarrhea and influenza due to prolonged lack of clean drinking water and poor sanitation and hygiene.

He is now appealing to the Member for Sinasina-Yongomugl, Hon. Kerenga Kua and the District Development Authority to assist immediately.

Kua noted that the Marape-Rosso National Government had allocated K300 million nationwide for El Nino relief in the recent Supplementary Budget, and said the people of SSY are waiting urgently for relief assistance.

Efforts to get comments from the SSY DDA and Provincial Disaster Office are continuing.

item.title: Milne Bay PEC assists schools to complete academic year amid El Nino

item.content:encoded: ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Government has come to the aid of schools in Milne Bay province affected by the onset of the El Nino'. ‎They've allocated K1.2mil this week to assist schools to complete the 2026 academic year, particularly boarding schools and students preparing to sit for the upcoming National Examinations. ‎ ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Executive Council (PEC) met on Thursday evening to discuss assistance for schools affected by the El Nino' conditions following a policy submission from the Provincial Division of Education. ‎ ‎Milne Bay Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, told NBC News yesterday that a submission was presented to the Provincial Government for assistance, especially with the National Examinations coming up for the grades 10s and 12s. ‎ ‎"The cabinet saw that it's very important for schools to complete their 2026 academic year, mainly the grades 10s and 12s in boarding schools. The cabinet in it's wisdom endorsed a total of K1.2mil for the rescue of all the schools affected by the El Nino". Magiodu said. ‎ ‎He said because of the urgency and difficulties associated with normal procurement processes, affected schools and boarding institutions have been asked to submit their quotations and requirements for assistance. ‎ ‎ ‎Magiodi said the payment will be made to suppliers based on the submitted requirements to allow schools to access the assistance. ‎

item.title: Ume is new BX-9 interim Welterweight champion
item.description: PNG boxer John Ume, aka the Ring Monster, is now the BX-9 interim Welterweight champion after defeating Hamzy Perwaisy last night in Auckland by technical knockout in the seventh round. The earlier rounds were even as both Ume and Perwaisy exchanged jabs to score.
item.content:encoded:
PNG boxer John Ume, aka the Ring Monster, is now the BX-9 interim Welterweight champion after defeating Hamzy Perwaisy last night in Auckland by technical knockout in the seventh round.

The earlier rounds were even as both Ume and Perwaisy exchanged jabs to score.

Ume was composed all through and pull off the show stopper in the seventh round to knock down the New Zealander.

Ume's next bout will be against Riley Allan for the Official Welterweight title early 2027.

Coach Peter Morrision said he is happy with the way Ume dominated the pace of the fight.

"His conditioning and fitness were outstanding and he executed the game plan we wanted,' Morrision said.

"We knew the opponent would be tough, so we prepared for a 10 x round war if required," he added.

Meanwhile in the cruiserweight, Kondup Samson Wailo went down to his opponent Duken Williams by TKO

Despite the loss, Wailo acknowledged all those who helped him to travel to New Zealand for his first International Professional Boxing bout.

item.title: Junior Kumuls create history
item.description: The Papua New Guinea Junior Kumuls have etched their names into the history books following first win 18-10 at the Santos National Football Stadium. Coach Joe Grima was positive throughout the week that the team was going to deliver which paid off today in the Nations Capital.
item.content:encoded:
The Papua New Guinea Junior Kumuls have etched their names into the history books following first win 18-10 at the Santos National Football Stadium.

Coach Joe Grima was positive throughout the week that the team was going to deliver which paid off today in the Nations Capital.

This marks the junior team their first of many to come as the Prime Minister XIIIs clashes continue this afternoon.

It was a slow start in the first 10 minutes of the match however, the Junior National team cruised past the Australian School Boys scoring their first try. It was their centre Jason Daniel who drew first blood for the home team.

The try was assisted by Co-captain Elijah Birve who also converted it at the far end of the field to take the lead.

Before half time, Junior Kumuls added double points to the board when Otto Thomas found his way through a tough defense. This helped the Junior Kumuls secure 10-0 lead at halftime.

In the second half it took a few minutes to settle before the Australian School Boys scored their first try. PNG extended through Daniel moments after to extend their lead.

The Australian School Boys added another however fell short. To secure a historic win, Birve converted a penalty goal to extend just three minutes before full time.

“We’ve been trying for about three or four years and there was something special about today and it’s hard to put it into words,” Grima said.

He said having a couple of elite junior players from the NRL pathway added the level of eliteness to this side while results of their academy program had a positive outcome from this historic win.

“We didn’t make the errors that we usually do, today we didn’t have to make the boys, because they knew what they were going to do out there and they delivered.”

Meanwhile Grima is positive that the next five years looks promising for the Junior Kumuls with the pathway now set for PNG.

item.title: IRC and NIO on joint operations
item.description: The Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) and the National Intelligence Office (NIO) will now be able to share information and intelligence on joint operations. This includes appropriate investigations, capacity building and technical cooperation, collaboration on cyber security, financial intelligence and Anti-money laundering and Counter Terrorism Financing frameworks.
item.content:encoded:
The Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) and the National Intelligence Office (NIO) will now be able to share information and intelligence on joint operations.

This includes appropriate investigations, capacity building and technical cooperation, collaboration on cyber security, financial intelligence and Anti-money laundering and Counter Terrorism Financing frameworks.

The partnership was sealed through a Memorandum of Understanding in Port Moresby yesterday.

Tax evasion, illicit financial flows, money laundering, terrorism financing, smuggling and corruption weakens the country's economy and its sovereignty.

This was highlighted by the Director General of the National Intelligence Office Eddie Yodu adding that it is a partnership between two organisations with different mandates, it serves a common purpose to protect the country as threats to national security are crosscutting.

“National security is everyone's responsibility. Today, the National Intelligence Organization and the Internal Revenue Commission are showing what that means in practice. This MOU sets out how we will work together.” Director Yodu said.

DIO Director said their partnership provides sharing of information and intelligence, joint operations and investigations where appropriate, capacity building and technical cooperation and collaboration on cyber security and financial intelligence.

“Where our work uncovers criminal conduct, we will refer matters to FASU, the constabulary or other competent authorities and agencies to deal with them effectively.” He said.

Yodu said everything done under this Mou will remain within the laws and within each agency's statutory mandate, with full respect for taxpayer confidentiality. Information shared between the two agencies will be protected.

The Internal Revenue Commission’s Commissioner General Sam Loi is grateful for this MOU which will allow joint risk assessments and operational working groups and intelligence including practices in how threats are being assessed and new capabilities.

Acting Commissioner General Internal Revenue Commission, Sam Loi confirmed that this is the way forward in trying to establish the connection.

“I think this is the way forward in trying to establish that connection where we are able to do our jobs more effectively without each of the relevant agencies trying to keep their own fence around it.” Acting Commissioner Loi said.

Both organisations noted that with this collaboration, they can do their jobs more effectively in addressing threats to the country’s revenue.

item.title: Madang Government gives K500,000 to upgrade school
item.description: The Madang Provincial Government has given K500, 000 to Madang Technical College, towards the college's initial preparations on becoming a Polytechnical college in the near future. Mr Pariwa was at the college yesterday and presented a dummy cheque plus the remittance advice stating that the money has been deposited into the college's account.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Government has given K500, 000 to Madang Technical College, towards the college's initial preparations on becoming a Polytechnical college in the near future.

Mr Pariwa was at the college yesterday and presented a dummy cheque plus the remittance advice stating that the money has been deposited into the college's account.

At hand, to receive the dummy cheque was Deputy Principal- Administration, Robert Turik, and members of the college's Governing Council, Henry Kambuka and Alex Paira, witnessed by staff and students.

Mr Pariwa made a commitment last year that he would return to school, and he did yesterday with the dummy cheque.

"I decided to come back and support this institute because Madang Technical College is a distinguished institution of higher technical learning in the province. If we are serious about building the nation, then Madang Technical College is an institute of nation-building, so we must invest in it.

"I am proud to say that Madang Technical College is my highest technical learning institution in the province. I must look around in the province to ensure we build the capacity of the institution to empower the learning environment build and instill skills into our youth population," Pariwa said.

He added that whilst a lot of students get into primary schools through to high and secondary schools, not a lot get into universities because of the system and the capacity to accommodate the entire students.

Once updagraded to a polytechnical college, the institute can introduce more technical courses than what it is already offering.

Governor Pariwa further emphasized that if we truly want to build this nation, we must invest in human resources.

Mr Pariwa reiterated that his commitment to education is a priority, adding work on uplifting the level of Madang Technical College into a Polytechnical college starts now.

"It cannot happen overnight, but it has to start somewhere, somehow and it has started now. We will upscale the level with or without the support of the National Government because I have had enough of talks," Governor Pariwa said.

Meanwhile, Deputy Principal, Administration, Robert Turik commended Governor Pariwa for his government's support to the college.

Mr Turik also took the opportunity to highlight a new concept that Madang Technical College has embarked on to help create pathways for students in vocational schools around the country.

The concept is called Downlinking and Uplinking.

Turik explained, "We have gone out to several vocational schools in the province and outside including a study centre in Manus and a vocational school on Rabaul. Next, we are going to Tari. The Downlinking concept is to create pathways for the students as per the government's policy on leaving no one behind."

"So the students that don't go through the formal way of education, we are creating that pathway for them in accordance with the Department of Higher Education's PNG National Qualification Framework, which includes 11 steps from level one certificate to masters and doctorate level. So we are giving the chance competitively.

"When we downlink with a FODE or vocational school, their students have the opportunity to come through us and go out to pursue their studies in universities."

He added that FODE and vocational colleges are no longer second opportunities.They provide the same privileges as universities.

Under Uplinking, the college is creating Memorandums of Understanding or relationships with universities and other stakeholders.

Currently, the college has created an MOU with Divine Word University to help the students achieve the three years National Qualification Framework.

The program assists the students progress from level 1 certificate to diploma, degree, masters and even doctorate.

A similar MOU was recently signed with Ramu NiCo.

Alex Paira, a member of the college's Governing Council applauded Mr Pariwa and his government for honouring the commitment.

He said, "Your commitment to Madang Tech is now becoming obvious that you are serious, unlike other MPs who made commitments but never came back. So we at Madang Tech, we just have to make sure we do our part."

Mr Paira urged the college to be accountable, stressing that K500, 000 is a lot of money.

item.title: KCH strengthens Governance capability through training
item.description: Kumul Consolidated Holdings (KCH) has completed its fourth Director Development Program, equipping 17 middle management personnel from State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) with skills to strengthen governance and prepare for potential future board roles. KCH Managing Director Professor, David Kavanamur presented certificates to participants at the conclusion of the three-day program, held from 28 to 30
item.content:encoded:
Kumul Consolidated Holdings (KCH) has completed its fourth Director Development Program, equipping 17 middle management personnel from State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) with skills to strengthen governance and prepare for potential future board roles.

KCH Managing Director Professor, David Kavanamur presented certificates to participants at the conclusion of the three-day program, held from 28 to 30 September 2026 at the Aviat Club in Port Moresby.

Delivered by the PNG Institute of Directors (PNGID), with support from the Asian Development Bank’s Pacific Private Sector Development Initiative (ADB-PSDI), the program brought together 10 men and seven women nominated by PNG Ports, PNG DataCo, MVIL, Air Niugini, Kumul Agriculture and PNG Power.

Professor Kavanamur said the participants formed part of a growing pool of prospective directors whose skills, experience and merit could contribute to SOE boards.

“You are here because your organisations see in you the judgement, integrity and potential to take on greater responsibility,” he said.

Established in 2021, the program was designed to strengthen governance capability and increase women’s representation on SOE boards. The first three cohorts trained 65 women, several of whom have since served as directors.

This year’s fourth cohort included male participants for the first time, extending the initiative to develop governance capability among SOE personnel.

The program covered directors’ duties, the respective roles of boards and management, strategy, financial oversight, risk, accountability and effective boardroom conduct.

Professor Kavanamur encouraged participants to apply their learning immediately in their current roles.

“Use these skills now, instead of waiting for a Board appointment. In your current roles, you can ask better questions, use resources responsibly, raise concerns early and make decisions with integrity,” he said.

He thanked PNGID and ADB-PSDI for their continued support and acknowledged the participating SOEs for enabling their staff to attend.

item.title: Dr. Waiye murder case adjourned to Monday
item.description: The seven suspects in the murder case of the late Dr. Robert Waiye have been remanded at the Barawagi Correctional Institution after their first court mention today. The suspects, who have been in custody at the Kundiawa Police Station cells since 17th September, appeared before Senior Provincial Magistrate Edward Kupo at the Kundiawa District Court at 1:00 PM today.
item.content:encoded:
The seven suspects in the murder case of the late Dr. Robert Waiye have been remanded at the Barawagi Correctional Institution after their first court mention today.

The suspects, who have been in custody at the Kundiawa Police Station cells since 17th September, appeared before Senior Provincial Magistrate Edward Kupo at the Kundiawa District Court at 1:00 PM today.

The accused are Emmanuel Wax, 32, Sandra (Emmanuel) Limbia, 30, Sogan Dilu, 32, Moses John, 25, Kailo Andy, 25, Benjamin Kuat, 25, and Polly (Boi) Kaman, 30.

Magistrate Kupo explained the police allegations to the accused and ordered that all seven be charged under one joint charge.

He directed the Criminal Investigation Division and the arresting officer to finalize all charges over the weekend and present the completed file before the court on Monday, 5th October 2026.

Magistrate Kupo further ruled that any application for bail is a matter for the National Court.

The court precinct was packed with Simbu Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Mazuc Rubiang, police personnel, relatives of the late Dr. Waiye, the legal team of the Simbu Provincial Health Authority, and members of the general public who turned up to witness the first mention.

All seven accused have been transferred from the Kundiawa Police cells and remanded in custody at Barawagi Correctional Institution pending their next court appearance.
